key_insight: CoorDex shows that humanoids can learn to move and manipulate continuously, rather than freezing to grasp objects. It coordinates whole-body motion and dexterous hand control through a shared latent residual policy, enabling more natural high-DoF loco-manipulation.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the common limitation in humanoid robotics where locomotion and manipulation are treated separately: robots walk to an object, stop, grasp with simple low-DoF end effectors, and then resume moving. It aims to enable continuous, on-the-move manipulation with dexterous hands and coordinated body control.
method: Learns a coordinated latent residual control policy that maps high-dimensional body and hand commands into a compact action space.
Combines body priors and hand priors so locomotion and dexterous manipulation can be optimized together instead of independently.
Uses simulation-based training to produce a controller capable of continuous humanoid loco-manipulation in dynamic tasks.
impact: For AI and robotics practitioners, CoorDex suggests a practical path toward more capable humanoid systems that can act in real-world settings without interrupting motion. This can improve efficiency, fluidity, and task performance in service, warehouse, and assistive robotics.

paper_title: CoorDex: Coordinating Body and Hand Priors for Continuous Dexterous Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
paper_authors: Sikai Li, Shuning Li, Zhenyu Wei, Yunchao Yao, Chenran Li
